newsitem.title: ITALY: Pope John Paul leaves for Sarajevo.
newsitem.headline: Pope John Paul leaves for Sarajevo.

text.p: Pope John Paul left Rome on Saturday for an historic visit to Sarajevo, only hours after mines connected to a detonator were discovered under a bridge in the Bosnian capital.

The 76-year-old Pontiff, leader of the world's Roman Catholics, took off on a special Alitalia flight from Rome's Fiumicino airport. He was expected to arrive in Sarajevo shortly before 6.00 p.m. (1600 GMT).
A Bosnian police officer said 23 mines, believed to have been recently planted and linked to a remote control system, had been found under a bridge on a main boulevard in the city.
Sarajevo authorities declined to comment on whether the Pope's motorcade planned to pass along the road, but visiting dignitaries usually use it to and from the airport.

The Pope is expected to appeal during his 25-hour trip for forgiveness and co-existence among Catholic Croats, Moslems and Orthodox Serbs to help cement a fragile peace since the end of a war that fed on ethnic and religious hatreds.
The Pope tried to visit Sarajevo in September 1994 when the war was raging but had to cancel the trip because Serb forces laying siege to the city refused to give security guarantees.
